proof_readings.assessment: The exact coset hypothesis is G1 distinct intersections, G2 residual generation and G3 common representatives. The subgroup induction uses a finite type set but not a finite ambient group. These unchanged interfaces were reread, and their previous complete independent acceptance is reused. No C-group or flag-transitivity conclusion is inferred from arbitrary coset data alone.

Finite pairwise intersection sizes force precisely the prescribed nesting/disjointness, including repeated and empty sets. Distinct proper selected containers form a laminar inclusion forest. Its difference atoms have equal cardinalities; the root atom contains Q and equals the complement of the selected targets. Any prescribed injection extends on that atom. If a selected set is all Omega, Q is empty; discarding that vacuous constraint removes the apparent root-atom exception. No freedom on the prescribed local map is lost.

For the left action convention, realizations are g0 K with K stabilizing every standard selected subset and fixing every point of the prescribed domain. Thus chi(g0)^(-1)c must lie in chi(K). This is exact for an arbitrary target group C, and does not assert arbitrary parity can always be chosen.

The common refinement of two forest component partitions equals the components of their common edges, by unique tree paths. Internal block permutations and cross-edge transpositions generate every component symmetric group. New flag completion invokes UB.Laminar with empty Q. Nonempty finite blocks ensure strictness/distinct intersections; rank-at-least-two residues have their stated generation. Isolated components contribute the same nonfaithful kernel as before.

Choose a minimal quotient-generating subfamily T, replace each other generator by s w_s^-1, and use substitution to preserve irredundance relative to T. For an abelian kernel, G=N<T> makes the ambient conjugation action equal the base action on N; no splitting is used. This is now a single proof of the Cameron-Cara inequality used by B2 and the all-degree bounds. The eight inherited Lean statements verify normalization/conjugation, not the cardinality inference or module bounds.

A family of s irredundant module generators gives a surjection onto s simple quotients by the maximal-omission construction. If its generated submodule is a proper hyperplane and s>=m-1, all simple factors are trivial and it would lie in the one-dimensional fixed space. For the full permutation module, there is only one independent trivial quotient, so m>=2s-1. The inequality floor((m+1)/2)<=m-2 includes m=4. For S_m a nonconstant vector produces all e_i+e_j, giving the stronger bound two. Hence a proper block image costs at most 2m-4, and the full block image costs at most m+1<2m-2 even at m=4. This proof does not use the later extremal classification.

The complete prior proof remains: signed cyclic ternary and binary degree-nine modules; block sizes two/three/four; exact bounded primitive exceptions; original Maroti lower-containment alternatives and integer envelope; simple subdirect-product partition chain and normalization; primitive block stabilizer bounds; then all minimal-block size/number cases, including m=2 and degree-six S5. I reread these complete arguments. The retained catalogue/classical facts and prior independent finite replay remain required, not replaced by the new degree-four tests.

The even-word identity tau_e tau_f=(s tau_e)^-1(s tau_f) proves each sign-generated subgroup, including the empty support where <s> intersect Alt is trivial. Intersect the actual K_F groups and the parity conditions. Independence and full generation are proved separately. Inverting an individual generator preserves its cyclic subgroup, so every allowed orientation is covered.

W1 gives full Sn generation; separately retained W2 plus the binary obstruction leaves intransitive omissions or one An omission. The chosen orbit-crossing edges form a spanning tree. Its cut intersections recover each generator as a transposition or one of the stated even two-edge elements. Relative independence then forces B into maximal omission groups; a nondistinguished pendant fixes a point, excluding the half-swapping coset at every balanced cut. Full intersection gives B=1. No independence/IP premise is silently upgraded.

The three counts remain distinct: actual ordinary sets, actual sign sets, and independent inversion classes. Canonical multiplication by the unique odd transposition identifies the switched-edge tree. Existence uses UB.F, the actual surjective stabilizer sign image and the complete residue maximality argument. The converse for arbitrary firm/RC/FT geometries still treats the possible single balanced overgroup, recovers all panel groups, then uses G2 downwards. It does not assume residual weak primitivity in that last direction. W1/W2, Cayley and inner automorphisms stay retained.

Apply the arbitrary-element UB.Extremal. A tree on at least three vertices has an edge adjacent to its distinguished edge; the corresponding sign mark has order three. Therefore an involution marking must be the ordinary tree. UB.F, UB.Coset and adjacency propagation supply all intersections, thinness, residual connectivity and the full type-preserving automorphism group. Thus the former independent maximum-rank proof has genuinely been replaced by an application of the shared theorem.

All mixed identities H_S intersect Y(pi_R), partition meets and one-extra-point saturation remain explicit. The root is a leaf; when both root components are nontrivial their intersection contains its unique first edge. The one-singleton case uses the mixed core identity, not a false claim that the core itself is Young. UB.F replaces only the common forest-refinement argument. All three actual four-letter cores are verified; their failure with two root edges remains a literal counterexample.

The complete prior necessity proof is unchanged and was reread: selected orbit-crossing forest, two components, possible extra-edge configurations, uniform splitting identities, all five-letter path/star extensions, long repetitions, parallel-edge exclusion and exactly one attachment. The argument is exhaustive for n>=9 because any five-letter core has an edge to the complement; finite examples do not prove completeness. The distinct endpoint/middle orbits of the D8 core and the transitive V4 core produce precisely A/B/C.

Actual cosets are subsets, pairs/ordered data and a four-point bridge decoration. The finite decoration proof constructs a simultaneous bijection on Q for every subset of local types. If no bridge is selected, the support uses at most three points and extends into a four-subset of D. Every ordinary tree subset is outside Q, and |D|>=4. Therefore the exact arbitrary injection furnished by the local proof satisfies UB.Laminar; mere existence of some root map would not suffice. All residue/panel and full automorphism consequences remain proved.

The complete tree presentation and two-sided presentation transport are retained verbatim. The explicit A/B/C inverse words recover all tail/core transpositions under arbitrary branching. The literal Corollary6.5(2) commutation claim remains refuted; the exact corrected general presentation is claimed instead. The n=8 example retains its required auxiliary program, including actual transitive parabolic order1344. The exact historical C-rank table and unfixed leaf-count convention remain excluded.
